title: The Magic of Miami Beach
description: Before celebrities, nightclubs, and luxury resorts, Miami Beach was a shifting world of mangroves, coral, water, and extraordinary biodiversity. This exhibit explores the forgotten history of the countless workers who transformed the landscape of Miami Beach and whose names rarely appear in the official histories. Through photographs the convergence of geology, ecology, labor, memory, and imagination forms a new image of the iconic beachside. For more information, please contact the branch at (305) 535-4219 or fuenteso@mdpls.org. All ages.
long_description:
Before celebrities, nightclubs, and luxury resorts, Miami Beach was a shifting world of mangroves, coral, water, and extraordinary biodiversity.

On this narrow barrier island, sand and limestone formed a dynamic ecosystem that would later be transformed through the labor of countless workers whose names rarely appear in official histories.

Taking Collins Park as its point of departure, this exhibition looks beyond the familiar story of one of America's best-known tourist destinations to explore the intertwined histories of nature and human labor. It considers how geology, ecology, and the work of largely invisible laborers shaped the city that emerged during the early twentieth century.

As John Collins, Thomas Pancoast, and Carl Fisher pursued their vision for Miami Beach, mangrove forests were cleared, sand was dredged from Biscayne Bay, and limestone fill was transported to create roads, homes, hotels, and public buildings. Fossilized coral limestone quarried at Windley Key became a defining architectural material, cladding landmarks such as today's Bass Museum, while coconut palms and monumental baobab trees helped construct the tropical environment they envisioned.

The catalyst for this project was a single 1924 photograph of a Black laborer standing among towering mangroves, reproduced in the 1938 book The Magic of Miami Beach. That image prompted an exploration of archival photographs, mangrove ecosystems, and fossilized coral, uncovering histories embedded within the island itself.

The works in this exhibition invite visitors to look beneath Miami Beach's familiar surface and reconsider the forces that shaped it. Here, the island's enduring magic is found not in the mythology of tourism, but in the convergence of geology, ecology, labor, memory, and imagination.

title: Energy, Chaos, & Transformation
description: This exhibition brings together a selection of contemporary abstract works that explore the visible and invisible forces shaping the human experience. Kemelmajer invites viewers to experience abstraction not only through what they see, but through what they feel. Each work becomes a space for personal interpretation, where individual memories and emotions can shape meaning. For more information, please contact the branch at 305-553-1134 or fuenteso@mdpls.org. All ages.
long_description:
Energy, Chaos & Transformation brings together a selection of contemporary abstract works by Carina Kemelmajer that explore the visible and invisible forces shaping the human experience.

The exhibition unfolds as a journey. On the lower level, vibrant color, layered textures, gestural marks, and dynamic compositions create an immediate sense of movement and intensity. Lines intersect, forms collide, and color expands across the surface, suggesting moments when life feels unpredictable, accelerated, and in constant motion. Chaos, however, is not presented as disorder alone, but as a space of possibility—a place where change can begin.

As the eye moves upward, the visual language shifts. Color gives way to a more restrained palette of black, white, and gray. Here, energy becomes quieter but no less present. Through contrast, texture, fragmented forms, and layered structures, these works explore the intangible forces that influence our lives: memory, perception, emotion, time, and the invisible boundaries that guide or challenge us.

Across both levels, opposing forces continually meet: energy and stillness, structure and freedom, light and darkness, rupture and reconstruction. Rather than resolving these tensions, Kemelmajer allows them to coexist, reflecting transformation as an ongoing human process rather than a final destination.

The exhibition invites viewers to experience abstraction not only through what they see, but through what they feel. Each work becomes a space for personal interpretation, where individual memories and emotions can shape meaning.

Ultimately, Energy, Chaos & Transformation is a reflection on movement through uncertainty—and on our capacity to transform experience into awareness, resilience, and new possibilities.

title: The Firmament
description: The Firmament begins with the natural development of consciousness and considers how our internal worlds are shaped through continuous exchange with family, geography, architecture, education, media, technology, and social expectations. Through large impressive oil paintings, the viewer is taken on a journey as they ask themselves, how much of what we call reality has been given to us, and how much have we assembled through the act of looking? For more information, please contact the branch at 305-553-1134 or fuenteso@mdpls.org. All Ages.
